summary: Staggered short-lived connection fanout causing autoscaler telemetry silence and transient GPU shortages
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden ~30-60% drop in sustained throughput for their dedicated pool for short intervals (5-12 minutes) around 11:00 and 15:00 UTC on 2026-02-18. Immediate symptom: requests queue and p99 token latency spikes while total GPU allocation appears normal, and autoscaler does not add burst capacity during the window (no scale-up events recorded).

Impact: Production request latency degradation for several customer-critical endpoints; Strategram Analytics reports degraded SLA for inference-heavy dashboards. Multiple internal customers share this reserved pool; customer is on a dedicated plan and expects guaranteed throughput.

Environment: Dedicated reserved cluster (pool-id: pool-7a3f), mixed-GPU cluster (A100 + H100 nodes), prod regions: us-west-2 primary, eu-west-1 failover. Observed against redwood/gpt-8x pinned to v1.2.

Initial detection: Customer alerted Support (SUP) via console alert at 2026-02-18T11:07Z. Support created ticket at 11:18Z and escalated to SRE/Serving.

Observed behavior details:
- Short-lived connection fanout pattern: heavy number of concurrent short streams (<10s each) from a small set of tenant connections producing many small, cold batches.
- Serving runtime shows KV cache churn and high per-request setup overhead despite apparent available GPU slots.
- Autoscaler telemetry ingestion pipeline exhibited an intermittent telemetry gap (11:06–11:12 and 15:02–15:10 UTC) which suppressed scale decisions.

Why this is unusual: Normally the autoscaler would detect burst pressure and provision a burst node or increase pooling. Here telemetry silence combined with noisy small-stream mix prevented autoscaler from triggering and allowed short lived tenant bursts to saturate batchers and produce p99 latency spikes despite aggregate capacity available.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a test tenant mapped to pool-7a3f in prod-us-west-2
2) Fire 200 concurrent short-lived streaming requests (each ~3-8s) across 50 client connections, staggered to create fanout spikes every 30s
3) Observe serving-runtime metrics: kv_cache_evictions, batch_wait_time, active_slots
4) Watch autoscaler metrics and logs for scale decision events; note whether scale decisions are logged during fanout windows

investigation_notes: 11:20 - Collected customer request ids and pool assignment. Verified pinned model version and quota limits.
11:35 - Observed autoscaler telemetry gap in ingestion pipeline (kafka consumer lag spike) coincident with customer reported window. Consumer lag resolved automatically after ~6 minutes.
12:10 - Correlated pattern: many short-lived streams produce frequent KV cache churn; cache pressure amplified setup cost for each new stream, reducing batching efficiency.

12:45 - Hypothesis: telemetry silence prevented autoscaler from seeing instantaneous queue depth and request churn; autoscaler policy uses moving-window signals and suppressed decisions if key telemetry streams are missing.
13:50 - Verified that scheduler showed available GPU slots but batchers had high wait times due to fanout and serialization. This created effective slot starvation despite free GPU capacity.

15:20 - Identified two tenant connections (strat-01 and internal-test-09) responsible for >70% of short-stream fanout during incidents. These tenants have aggressive connection patterns not previously rate-limited.

15:45 - Confirmed autoscaler code path: when telemetry ingestion errors are observed, autoscaler enters a conservative hold for 10 minutes to avoid oscillation; this hold prevented responsive burst provisioning.
17:00 - Engagement with infra team: kafka consumer (autoscaler-telemetry) had transient GC stall and broker-side short spike; raised follow-up INT ticket for telemetry consumer resilience.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-02-18 11:18Z: Opened ticket after receiving customer alert. Gathered initial request ids and pool assignment. Escalated to SRE.
Lena Chen (SRE) 2026-02-18 11:40Z: Observed autoscaler telemetry consumer lag. Added temporary alert to detect consumer lag >30s. Noted correlation with p99 spikes.

Marco Reyes (Serving Eng) 2026-02-18 12:15Z: Confirmed KV cache churn and increased per-stream setup CPU. Suggested short-term workaround: apply tenant-level concurrency throttle and increase batcher max_batch_wait to 50ms for pool-7a3f.

Stratagem Analytics (customer) 2026-02-18 12:30Z: Provided client-side traces showing many short-lived connections started by their dashboard workers. Agreed to apply application-side backoff while we investigate.
Marco Reyes (Serving Eng) 2026-02-18 16:10Z: Deployed temporary rate-limit policy via console for tenant strat-01 and internal-test-09. Observed p99 drop from ~1.1s to ~220ms within 2 minutes.
SRE (Lena Chen) 2026-02-18 17:20Z: Applied consumer GC tuning to autoscaler-telemetry instance and increased consumer parallelism. Created INT ticket INT-9921 for durable fix.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-02-19 09:00Z: Customer confirmed no recurrence during peak window on 2026-02-19. Customer requested postmortem and mitigation plan.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: (1) Temporary tenant-level concurrency cap and small per-tenant burst token bucket applied to strat-01 and internal-test-09 to smooth short-stream fanout. (2) Batcher's max_wait configured to 50ms for pool-7a3f to improve coalescing of small streams. (3) Autoscaler telemetry consumer GC and parallelism fix merged (PR #1428) and deployed to autoscaler-telemetry in us-west-2. (4) Scheduled rebalancing of pool-7a3f to spread noisy tenants across additional nodes during peak hours.

Permanent follow-ups and action items:
- INT-9921: Hardening of telemetry ingestion (consumer resilience, backpressure handling, better alerts).
- Add autoscaler fallback that uses scheduler queue depth and batcher_wait_time as secondary signals when primary telemetry is missing.
- Implement per-tenant short-stream detection and automatic soft-throttling to avoid KV cache thrash.
- Postmortem planned for 2026-02-25; share link to postmortem and customer-facing RCA.

Customer impact: mitigated; SLA window impacted for short period 11:06–11:12 and 15:02–15:10 on 2026-02-18. Customer satisfied with temporary measures and requested timeline for permanent fixes.
notes: Follow-up: Coordinate with Product on default batcher max_wait and with Growth to communicate mitigation to other dedicated customers with similar traffic patterns.
